title: AI Models Research
summary: A research knowledge base for researchers, policy analysts and engineers comparing AI model families on capability, accuracy, speed, energy use and token cost, with every figure sourced, dated and graded.

narrative.problem: Public discussion of model capability is dominated by provider launch materials and single-number leaderboard rankings, often produced under evaluation conditions that are undisclosed, unreproducible, or not comparable across providers, so it is hard to choose a model for a given task, budget and deployment constraint on evidence.
narrative.decision: Separates independently verified measurement (Grade A), institutional primary research (Grade B) and provider-reported claims (Grade C), and generates every comparison table from source-linked CSV records that validation scripts check.
narrative.tradeoff: Claims that cannot meet the standard are recorded as 'Not publicly disclosed' or 'Insufficient independent evidence' rather than estimated, so many cells stay empty and no model ranking is published.
narrative.limitation: Research cut-off 2026-07-22. Phase 1 is complete; chapters, data and navigation are partial; the sixteen model-family profiles are not started; energy, latency and factuality datasets are empty; and the survey is not peer reviewed.
narrative.caveat: Prices, rankings and availability are historical records as of the cut-off date, not current facts; nothing here is legal, financial or procurement advice.
